publications.assertionSummary: Highlight 'A trusted neighbor': signed the 1645 petition and 'served as a witness and appraiser for other families' estates.'

incoming.explanation: Deed associates (Brackett, Rockwell) show community ties.
Serving as will witness and appraiser evidences trust.
Co-signing the 1646 meadows petition with the founding cohort is a documented act of town collective action, evidencing standing.

shortLabel: Recognised standing in the Braintree community

sources.excerpt: debts due … to Peter Brackett, Joseph Adams …
sources.locator: John Gurney Senr inventory and debts, Braintree, 16 March 1663

statement: John Gurney held recognised standing in the Braintree community — signing the 1645 plantation petition, serving as probate witness and inventory-taker for Gregory Baxter (1659), and appearing across a dense Braintree creditor network in his own 1663 estate accounts.
